supporting_observations.claim: The alerted connections in the available records go to update.ledgerlink.com through the organization's proxy and occur at approximately five-minute intervals: 13:39:27, 13:43:51, 13:48:52, 13:53:58, 13:59:14, 14:04:11, and 14:09:13 UTC.
The LedgerLink updater was launched from its inventoried path, and Sysmon attributes the repeated proxy connections to that process (PID 4152).

The observed destination, updater process, and roughly five-minute cadence match the organization's stated approved LedgerLink update-check behavior; this supports a benign disposition for the alerted activity.
One scheduled check received a proxy gateway error (503) at 13:53:58 UTC; later checks succeeded. The error alone does not indicate malicious activity.

known_telemetry_limitations: The available records show LedgerLink checks from 13:39:27 through 14:09:13 UTC, but do not show the alerted activity's purported start around 13:30 UTC. The supplied evidence therefore does not independently verify the entire alert interval. (T256-00207, T256-00477)

The proxy records identify the destination and connection metadata, but the LedgerLink sessions are logged as tunnels; the records do not expose the update response contents or an update-package hash. (T256-00207, T256-00298, T256-00411)
claims_not_established: The evidence does not establish what update content, if any, was returned by update.ledgerlink.com.
The evidence does not establish whether checks occurred between 13:30 and the first recorded check at 13:39:27 UTC.
unrelated_findings: Separate ticket: Firefox accessed a Google Sheets document and related Google Docs resources, which are outside the listed approved cloud-storage services. The records establish access, not upload or data transfer. (T256-00456, T256-00457, T256-00458, T256-00466, T256-00468, T256-00469, T256-00473)
Separate ticket: a Dropbox updater connection to desktop.dropbox.com was observed; the record does not establish that files were synced or transferred. (T256-00316, T256-00317)

Separate ticket: Cisco AnyConnect's user interface was launched, although the environment context says there is no VPN; these records do not show a VPN connection. (T256-00146, T256-00149, T256-00151)

Separate ticket: the user ran PowerShell with ExecutionPolicy Bypass on update-inventory.ps1, followed by creation of a temporary file. These records do not establish the script's contents or intent. (T256-00155, T256-00158)

Separate ticket: unusual workstation activity included DNS resolution of afemode.sunridge.local and a Power BI connection attempt to the resolved host on port 1433, plus database and system-enumeration tooling. These are not the LedgerLink connections that triggered this alert. (T256-00080, T256-00084, T256-00091, T256-00094, T256-00103, T256-00106, T256-00172, T256-00174, T256-00271, T256-00276, T256-00278)
